entries.source: E. Curzel and G. M. Varanini (eds.), La documentazione dei vescovi di Trento (XI secolo–1218), Bologna 2011; Document 68
entries.summary: At Bolzano, Egno of Eppan/Appiano conveys Castelvecchio and related holdings to Bishop Conrad of Trento, who grants the castle back under stated feudal terms. Henricus de Resebacho occurs in the witness list.
entries.latin: (SN) Anno dominice nativitatis millesimo centesimo nonagesimo quarto, indictione duodecima, | die sabati nono intrante iulio, in Bauçanoa), in ecclesia Sancte Marie. | In presentia domini Truconisb), domini Adelpreti de Portariolac) canonicorum, Egenonis | de Maço, Rodegerii de Meço, Petarini, Federici de Winecco, Cahelo|chid) et eius fratris Conradi, Gote salkie), Warnardi de eodem loco, Henrici de | Resebachof), Sikeri de Monte Albano, Rempretig) de Bauçanoa), Odolrici | de Grunspergoh), Gotesalkie) de Volenstaine, ad hoc testium rogatorum. | Ibique dominus Egeno comes de Piano, iure et nomine proprii, investivit dominum | Conradum, Dei gracia Tridentine sedis episcopum, de dosso uno quod appellatur Ca|stellum Vetus, quod vero est in pertinentia Piani, et de duabus curiis que sunt ibi | prope, que vero sunt sue sororis, si poteriti) dare, et si nequaquam poteritj) | dare, dare debebit duas alias curias eiusdem bonitatis, in dicto predicti | Cahelochid) et Tourengi, Odolrici de Grunspergoh), Gotesalkie) de Volensta|ine infra annum. Et ibik) incontinenti versa vice predictus dominus episcopus, iure | et nomine feodi, investivit predictum dominum comitem, recipientem pro se | et pro nepote suo, de predicto dosso cum illis duabus curiis, ita videlicet | fecit hanc investituram quod predictus comes in manifestis werris | episcopatus debet aperire eidem domino episcopo predictum castellum vel suis succe|ssoribus contra omnes homines excepto domino imperatore, ipso comite ma|nente in eo castello, si predictus dominus episcopus petierit vel sui successo|res. Etl) si vero non aperuerit predictum castellum, ut dictum est, ob hanc cau|sam ipse dominus comes iure et nomine pignoris investivit predictum | episcopum de scaria sua de Nano, quam dicebat esse suum alodium, et de alia | sua curia de Riedo, quam dicebat esse suum feodum de Casadeo. Et in|super predictus Odolricus insimul cum predicto comite investivit ipsum dominum | episcopum de omni eo quod habet et tenet ipse Odolricus in Serecpoilo. Tali vero | ordine fecerunt hanc investituram quod si ipse dominus comes non aperiret pre|dictum castellum, ut dictum est, predicto domino episcopo vel suis successoribus, | predictum pignus debet esse de Casadei; et dixit se possidere pro ipso domino | episcopo de predicto dosso cum illis duabus curiis, et si vero contigeritm) quod aperu|erit et ipse dominus episcopus vel eius successores non redderit, tunc curia | de Domo debet esse feodum predicti domini comitis. Et insuper ibiquen) predic|tus comes ad sancta Dei ewangelia iuravit quod numquam faciet aliquam ra|ssam cum comite Henrico suo avonculoo) de Piano nec cum suis filiis | pro suo facto contra episcopatum vel pro quocumque alio facto, sine fraude, et quod | non inpediet predictum pignus. Et iuravit quod faciet iurare infra | annum illos quos posuerit in predicto castello, taliter si offendide | rintp) predictum dominum episcopum vel eius successores de aliquo, rationem | debet facere ipse comes de eis sub se, et si forte ipsiq) non faci(ent) rati|onem sub eo infra tres menses, debent rationem facere sub predicto | domino episcopo vel eius successoribus. | Ego Bertramus, domini imperatoris Hen(rici) notarius, rogatus interfui et hoc | instrumentum, ut supra legitur, scripsi.
entries.english:
In the year of the Lord’s nativity 1194, indiction twelve, on Saturday, the ninth day of July, at Bolzano, in the church of Saint Mary. In the presence of Lord Trucus, Lords Adelpretus of Portariola, canons; Egno of Meço; Rodegerius of Meço; Petarinus; Federicus of Weineck; Caheloch and his brother Conradus; Gotesalc; Warnardus of the same place; Henry of Resebacho; Sikerus of Monte Albano; Rempreti of Bolzano; Odolricus of Grunspergo; Gotesalc of Volenstain, witnesses summoned for this purpose.

There Lord Count Egno of Eppan, by right and as his own property, invested Lord Conrad, by the grace of God bishop of the see of Trento, with a hill called Castelvecchio, which lies within the territory of Eppan, and with two estates nearby that belonged to his sister, if he could obtain them from her. If he could not, he was to give instead two other estates of equal value within one year, in the place of those named above, at Caheloch and Tourengus, Odolricus of Grunspergo and Gotesalc of Volenstain. Immediately there, in return, the aforesaid lord bishop, by right and in the name of a fief, invested the aforesaid lord count, who received for himself and his nephew, with the aforesaid hill and the two estates. He made this investiture on the condition that, in open wars of the bishopric, the aforesaid count must open the castle to the bishop or his successors against all men except the lord emperor, while the count himself remained in the castle, if the bishop or his successors requested it.

If he did not open the aforesaid castle as stated, then as security the count invested the bishop with his estate at Nano, which he claimed as his allodial property, and with another estate of his at Riedo, which he claimed to hold as a fief from Casadeo. In addition, the aforesaid Odolricus together with the count invested the bishop with everything Odolricus held and possessed at Serecpoilo. They made this investiture on the following terms: if the count did not open the castle to the aforesaid bishop or his successors as stated, the pledged property was to belong to Casadei; and the count declared that he held the aforesaid hill and the two estates for the bishop. If, however, it happened that he did open it and the bishop or his successors did not return the pledge, then the estate at Domo was to be the fief of the aforesaid count.

There also, the aforesaid count swore on the holy Gospels of God that he would never make any raid with Count Henry, his uncle, of Eppan, or with Henry’s sons, against the bishopric for his own cause or for any other cause, and that he would not obstruct the aforesaid pledge. He swore that within a year he would cause those whom he placed in the aforesaid castle to swear that, if they wronged the aforesaid bishop or his successors in any matter, the count himself would answer for them. If they failed to answer before him within three months, they were to answer before the aforesaid bishop or his successors. I, Bertramus, notary of Lord Emperor Henry, was present at the request of the parties and wrote this instrument as set out above.
